key_insight: Equivariant graph neural networks better capture material geometry and improve optical spectra prediction, especially in the low-energy range and for static real permittivity.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more accurate screening of optoelectronic materials for thin-film solar cells and other devices where optical response matters.
method: Adapted the equivariant GNN GotenNet for optical spectra prediction.
Evaluated the model on multiple datasets, including 10,533 structures with RPA-computed spectra.
Compared against state-of-the-art surrogate models using rotation-invariant scalar features.
evidence_signal: The model outperformed current state of the art, with the largest gains in the 0–8 eV range and for static real permittivity on the RPA dataset.
watch_item: Performance gains are demonstrated on benchmark datasets, so transfer to new chemistries, structures, or lower-data regimes may require additional validation.
paper_title: Equivariant Graph Neural Networks Improve Optical Spectra Prediction for Materials Screening
